## Notes

- $\mathbb{N}$ are the **natural numbers**: 1, 2, 3, ...
- $\mathbb{Z}$ are the **integers**: ... ,-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...
- $\mathbb{Q}$ are the **rational numbers**: commonly thought of as fractions or decimals with finite or repeating digits after the decimal point 
- $\mathbb{R}$ are the **real numbers**: includes decimals with non-repeating digits after the decimal point such as $\sqrt{2}$ and $\pi$
- We have the set inclusion
$$ \mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R}$$
i.e. each new set of numbers has the previous one sitting in it
- $x \in \mathbb{N}$ means $x$ is a natural number, similarly with 
$\mathbb{Z}, \, \mathbb{Q} , \, \mathbb{R}$
